pr_semantic_analysis.change_summary: The web client adds a service worker that intercepts image asset GETs, serves successful responses from a versioned browser cache, supports background preloading, and can abort in-flight image loads when viewers or thumbnails are destroyed. Production tooling also gains a command to stop the production Compose stack. Several end-to-end assertions were removed or relaxed, but the supplied post-change source does not establish a corresponding product behavior change.

behavior_changes.description: Once the service worker controls a page, matching original and thumbnail asset GETs can be returned from a deployment-versioned browser cache; cache misses are fetched and successful 200 responses are stored for later requests.
evidence: The fetch handler only intercepts GET paths matching asset original or thumbnail URLs.
immichAsset checks Cache Storage before fetching and stores status-200 responses.
Activation removes cache entries whose names differ from the current deployment cache.

citations.quoted_text: let response = useCache ? await cache.match(url) : undefined;

behavior_changes.description: Photo-viewer lookahead loading is now requested through a BroadcastChannel instead of creating an Image object directly, allowing the service worker to fetch and cache the requested image in the background.
evidence: The viewer sends each image URL through preloadImageUrl.
The service worker handles preload messages by invoking its asset-loading function.

behavior_changes.description: When a photo loader is cleaned up or a thumbnail action is destroyed, the client asks the service worker to abort a currently tracked fetch for that URL.
evidence: Both image components emit cancellation during cleanup.
The service worker looks up the URL in pendingLoads and aborts its controller.

behavior_changes.description: Operators can now stop the production Docker Compose stack, including orphaned containers, through the new prod-down Make target.
evidence: The target invokes docker compose down against the production Compose file.

important_symbols.reason: This is the central interception path controlling cache lookup, network fetching, response caching, failure handling, and in-flight request tracking.
It defines activation-time cache retention and currently operates across all cache names visible to the origin.
These functions form the asynchronous protocol between UI components and the service worker.
It changes photo navigation preloading from normal browser image loading to service-worker-mediated loading and adds cleanup cancellation.
Its action lifecycle now cancels loading by URL when a thumbnail is destroyed, which can interact with other consumers of the same URL.

investigation_hints.description: Trace how the framework builds, registers, updates, and activates this service worker, including whether it immediately controls existing tabs after skipWaiting and clients.claim.
Trace all producers and consumers of the immich BroadcastChannel protocol and determine whether URL cancellation is scoped to one component or shared among concurrent consumers and tabs.

Inspect the asset endpoint's authorization, request-header, range-request, and caching semantics because interception replaces the original Request with a fetch made from its URL and may serve a cached response without contacting the endpoint.
Check test coverage for loading indicators and download progress after the photo-viewer spinner test and shared-link DOWNLOADING assertion were removed.

local_risks.description: Plausible authorization/cache-isolation defect: the cache is keyed by URL and a hit is returned without revalidating against the asset endpoint. If authentication state or users change while an asset URL remains reusable, a response cached under an earlier session could still be returned from browser storage.

citations.quoted_text: let response = useCache ? await cache.match(url) : undefined;

local_risks.description: Cancellation is URL-global rather than consumer-scoped. If multiple components or tabs request the same asset URL, destroying one component can abort the controller currently stored for another consumer, causing that intercepted request to receive an error response.

The intercepted network operation is reconstructed from only the URL instead of forwarding event.request. Requests that depend on original headers or options, such as range or conditional requests, can therefore return different content or status behavior.

Activation deletes every origin cache except the current deployment cache, without restricting deletion to this service worker's cache-name namespace. That can remove Cache Storage entries owned by other functionality sharing the origin.

affected_boundaries.uncertainty: The actual fetch-event listener and automatic registration of this service-worker entry are not supplied, and whether pages are controlled and issue matching requests remains runtime-dependent.

affected_boundaries.label: Component-to-service-worker image control helpers
evidence: The established call edge `preload -> preloadImageUrl` at `web/src/lib/components/asset-viewer/photo-viewer.svelte:72` crosses from the viewer component into `sw-messaging.ts`.

`preloadImageUrl` and `cancelImageUrl` are supplied changed production symbols in `web/src/lib/utils/sw-messaging.ts`.
affected_boundaries.reason: Viewer and thumbnail components cross into a shared messaging callable surface to request background image preloading or cancellation.
affected_boundaries.uncertainty: The supplied context does not establish whether other callers use these helpers or whether all target browsers support the underlying BroadcastChannel behavior.

affected_boundaries.label: Service-worker preload and cancellation message handling
evidence: The supplied behavior facts state that photo-viewer lookahead loading is requested through a BroadcastChannel and that cleanup asks the service worker to abort the tracked fetch for a URL.

The changed `pendingLoads` symbol in `web/src/service-worker/index.ts` concretely supports service-worker tracking of the loads controlled by those messages.
